title: [NPU] Backport PR #36426 to fix ModelSlim weight mappings and Qwen vision loading on the release branch
body:
# Motivation

This is a temporary patch for ModelSlim loading on the release branch. It backports the fixes from [sgl-project/sglang#36426](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36426) through `8786461`, leaving the broader mapping cleanup for follow-up work.

Missing mappings could select the wrong quantization settings, causing dtype mismatches and skipped scales. This change adds the Qwen GDN mappings while preserving existing fused names, and passes the quantization config to Qwen3-VL's vision model. It also flattens higher-dimensional inputs for the W8A8 linear operation and restores the output shape.

Compared the release branch before and after the patch using metadata and weight headers from 40 checkpoint samples. These provide the tensor names, shapes and dtypes needed to run loading checks with meta tensors, without loading the full weights into device memory.

| Models checked | Mapping / dtype result |
| --- | --- |
| Qwen3.8-27B W8A8, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MXFP8 | Fixed the loading errors; both checks pass |
| Qwen3-VL-8B / 30B-A3B W8A8 | Fixed the visual weight dtype errors and skipped inputs; other parameter warnings remain |
| Qwen3.8-27B BF16, Qwen3-Next original / W8A8, Qwen2.5-VL-7B W8A8 | Checks pass before and after |
| GLM-5 / 5.1 / 5.2 originals | Checks pass before and after |
| GLM-5.3-Flash, Kimi-K3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash originals | Same input mappings and dtypes before and after |
| Other GLM, Kimi-K2 and DeepSeek V3 / R1 samples | No new differences in completed checks; some checks remain blocked |
| DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1-Flash W8A8 | Existing loading/config errors remain |

Four Qwen samples improved, with no new mapping/dtype regressions observed in the covered paths. Some fused-scale checks assume compatible scale values. This validation covers loading metadata; device inference and the forward computation were not tested.

Resolve split GDN and vision quantization names while preserving checkpoints that already use fused names. Pass ModelSlim configuration to Qwen3-VL vision construction and flatten/restore higher-rank W8A8 linear inputs.

title: [NPU] Fix DeepSeek-V4 hc_pre in dual-machine PD disaggregation on Ascend 950
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 pre-processes each layer's mHC residual with a single fused op,
`torch.ops.custom.npu_hc_pre` (from `cann-recipes-infer`). **Running DeepSeek-V4
with dual-machine PD disaggregation (prefill/decode separation) on Ascend 950
fails on this path** — `hc_pre` raises an error during the disaggregated run.

<!-- paste the exact error / traceback here once captured -->

Ascend 950 (NPU arch35) also ships the official, CANN-maintained ops
`torch_npu.npu_mhc_pre` + `torch_npu.npu_mhc_sinkhorn`. This PR routes `hc_pre`
through those on 950 to fix the PD-disaggregation failure, while A2/A3 keep the
legacy `custom.npu_hc_pre` path unchanged.


Two API facts shape the implementation:

- The legacy fused op returns `(y, post, comb)`, and its `comb` is already
  Sinkhorn-normalised.
- The official `npu_mhc_pre` returns `h_res` **before** the Sinkhorn transform,
  so `comb` must be produced by chaining `npu_mhc_sinkhorn` (the old op did this
  inline). A naive op-name swap would silently feed a non-normalised `comb` into
  `hc_post`.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

1. `python/sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/mhc.py`
   - `npu_hc_pre` is now an arch dispatcher:
     - On Ascend 950 (`is_npu_arch35()`): `torch_npu.npu_mhc_pre(x, hc_fn, hc_scale, hc_base, gamma=None, norm_eps=rms_norm_eps, hc_eps=hc_eps, out_flag=0)` → `(h_in, h_post, h_res)`, then `torch_npu.npu_mhc_sinkhorn(h_res, eps=hc_eps, num_iters=hc_sinkhorn_iters)` → `comb`. `gamma=None` because the legacy op's RMS is unweighted (the caller applies `input_layernorm` separately).
     - On A2/A3: the legacy `custom.npu_hc_pre` call, **unchanged**.
   - The 4-tuple return contract `(y, post, comb, norm_fused=False)` and the idle/empty short-circuit are preserved.
   - `inner_precise` is intentionally not passed: older `torch_npu` builds do not declare it, and where it exists its default is `0` (FP32).
<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
### Scope note

- **A2/A3 keep the exact legacy path** — they never import `torch_npu`. Only 950 (arch35) takes the new branch.
- `hc_post` is intentionally **not** changed: it already has its own arch35 branch and consumes `(post, comb)`, whose shape/dtype are unchanged. The `custom` extension remains a dependency on 950 (via `custom.npu_hc_post`), which is fine for this change.
- Out of scope (possible follow-up): migrating `hc_post` to `torch_npu.npu_mhc_post`.

title: [NPU] Delegate CP token slicing to the CP-v2 strategy
body:
## Summary

Refactor the Ascend NPU prefill-CP attention path so token slicing / padding is delegated to the CP-v2 strategy instead of being re-implemented in the backend.

## Background

`do_cp_attn_fia` (in `ascend_backend.py`) re-implemented the prev/next zigzag token slicing, pad-row trimming, and pad-row re-appending that `ZigzagCPStrategy.run_attention` already owns. This replaces that duplication with a thin FIA computation closure passed to `run_attention`: the backend now only supplies the kernel, and the strategy owns the CP layout and padding.

title: [NPU] Fix uninitialized vision attention padding for MiniCPM-V-2.6
body:
## Motivation

Companion fix for `release/2026930` to upstream PR https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43748.

MiniCPM-V-2.6 pads image slices to the largest patch count in the batch. `VisionAscendAttention` removes those padded rows before FIA, then scatters the compact result into an output allocated with `torch.empty_like(q)`. Only valid rows are written, so padding retains uninitialized memory (or stale graph workspace contents).

During an Ascend A3 reproduction, one image produced slice lengths `[1014, 1036, 1036]`: 3086 valid rows in a 3108-row padded tensor. The first vision attention output had no nonfinite values in valid rows but 49 in padding. Nonfinite values subsequently appeared in the resampler output, and greedy decoding repeated `!` without reaching EOS. Requests without an explicit output limit continued decoding.

## Modifications

- Zero the padded output before restoring FIA results, for both multiple sequences and a single padded sequence. The unpadded path continues returning the FIA output directly.
- Add deterministic regression coverage using NaN-filled allocations and graph workspaces. Check valid Q/K/V packing, restored results, and zero padding across eager, metadata, and graph paths, including an unpadded control.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
python -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_vision_backend_selection.py -q
```

- Ascend `release/2026930` vision attention source: **19 passed** with the fix.
- The 9 added parameter combinations against the original implementation: **6 failed, 3 passed**. All padded combinations fail; unpadded controls pass.
- Ascend A3 / CANN 9.1.0 B083 image (`8b3bf500d746d3140e8b25332d2207429aab0373`) with this runtime fix: all **6 MiniCPM-V-2.6 tests passed in 96.231 s**, including mixed batch, single image, multiple images, multiple turns, video, and prefix cache reuse. Used the `TestMiniCPMV4Server` class from the Ascend test module, whose model is MiniCPM-V-2.6, with local weights and the original generation limits. This end-to-end run validates the fix on the B083 runtime; the unit suite above validates the current target source.
- The previously failing single-image response completed naturally after 42 tokens with `finish_reason=stop`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput benchmark. The fix adds zeroing only when restoring a padded output. In the end-to-end run, the mixed-batch test completed in 7.839 s and the single-image test in 0.902 s.

title: Fix hellaswag preload IndentationError causing full-test 404 (rowanz DMCA)
body:
## Summary

`test_npu_basic_sanity.py` (full-1-npu-a3) fails in the full-test pipeline with:

```
requests.exceptions.HTTPError: 404 Client Error: Not Found for url:
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rowanz/hellaswag/master/data/hellaswag_val.jsonl
```

Seen in run [37605365300](https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/actions/runs/37605365300) (job 112739451597, PR #1292) and in every full-test run since 2026-09-14.

## Root cause

1. **rowanz/hellaswag was DMCA-taken-down on 2026-09-14** (wikihow): the whole repo is blocked, every raw URL 404s permanently. Not an environment flake.
2. PR #1292 already anticipated this and added a preload step in `_npu-pr-test-stage.yml` (generate `/tmp/hellaswag_val.jsonl` from HF `Rowan/hellaswag`; `download_and_cache_file` skips the download when the file exists). But the preload **silently failed**:

```
File "<string>", line 2
    import json
IndentationError: unexpected indent
WARN: hellaswag preload failed; test_accuracy_floor will fail if /tmp file is absent
```

The multi-line `python3 -c "<...>"` inherits the YAML run-block indentation: every continuation line reaches python with leading spaces, so line 2 (`import json`) is indented -> IndentationError. The trailing `|| echo WARN` swallowed the failure, and `test_accuracy_floor` later hit the dead URL.

## Fix

`.github/workflows/_npu-pr-test-stage.yml` (nightly install step):

- Replace the inline multi-line `python3 -c` with a heredoc (`python3 - <<'PYEOF'`). Heredoc body lines are written at the run-block base indent (the `set -euo pipefail` level), so they start at column 0 after YAML strips the block indent, and `PYEOF` terminates at column 0.
- Overlay `python/sglang/test/kits/` + `test_programs.py` from the PR checkout (image snapshots may predate `kits/` / `test_hellaswag_select`), same intent as PR #1292.

## Verification

`.github/workflows/single-test-npu.yml` (verification-only, will be reverted after the CI result is reviewed):

- test case: `test/registered/npu/basic_function/speculative_inference/test_npu_basic_sanity.py`
- runs the same heredoc preload with fail-fast (this round exists to prove the preload code works), then the full case (`HellaswagMixin` 200q x2 via `sgl.select` + API-contract / decode-correctness / scheduler-stress mixins)

title: [NPU] Fix Gemma3 Q/K layout for Ascend FIA
body:
Gemma3 passes queries shaped `[1, num_tokens, num_heads, head_dim]` to attention. The Ascend FIA decode path reads `q.shape[0]` as the token count, so a batch of 64 tokens is interpreted as one token and can fail when allocating padding with a negative dimension (`-63`).

Normalize Gemma3 Q/K to the token-major, two-dimensional layout at the attention boundary on NPU, after Q/K normalization and RoPE. This fixes the input layout for FIA while keeping the shared Ascend attention backend unchanged. Other devices retain their existing layout.

Validation:
- A CPU regression harness executes the Gemma3 native forward path, native normalization/eager RoPE, and the unchanged Ascend decode implementation, with accelerator operations mocked.
- Reproduced the original negative-dimension failure before the change.
- Passed 14 NPU decode cases covering FIA and paged attention, float32/bfloat16, multiple batch sizes, and padding; 8 non-NPU layout/value comparisons; and 2 prefill attention-boundary cases (4 unittest methods in total).
- Import sorting, Ruff checks/formatting, AST, whitespace, merge-conflict, shebang, and repository-specific lint checks passed. Windows application control blocked some pre-commit launchers and the local hooks' `python3` alias was unavailable; the affected checks passed when invoked directly with the available Python interpreter.

Hardware validation on A3 host 151 (`Ascend910_9362`, CANN 9.1.0) at this PR head:
- FIA enabled, TP=4: passed a real 64-sequence decode smoke; probes confirmed token-major Q `[64, 512]` and the actual FIA operator call with Q `[64, 1, 2, 256]` / `BSND`.
- FIA enabled, TP=1: passed the original Gemma3 GSM8K case, accuracy **0.72 (144/200)** against threshold **0.70** (5-shot).
- FIA disabled, TP=2: all three original `TestGemmaUnderstandsImage` input-format methods passed (image, precomputed embeddings, processor output), with the original semantic assertions unchanged and decode probes confirming `use_fia=false`.

See the [hardware validation results and log excerpts](https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/pull/1320#issuecomment-6097566368) for environment and test-source details. MMMU benchmark accuracy and A5 hardware execution remain unvalidated.

title: [Fix] Adapt NPU Qwen-VL processor patch to transformers 5.19 resize() signature change
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Running Qwen2.5-VL / Qwen3-VL on NPU with transformers >= 5.19 crashes with: TypeError: Qwen2VLImageProcessor.resize() missing 2 required positional arguments: 'images' and 'factor' Transformers 5.19 refactored Qwen2VLImageProcessor.resize() and Qwen3VLVideoProcessor.resize():

- Old (<= 5.15): resize(image, size, resample) — the caller computed smart_resize() itself and passed the target SizeDict(height, width).
- New (5.19): resize(images, size, resample, factor[, temporal_factor]) -- smart_resize() moved inside resize(), which now takes the original size (shortest_edge/longest_edge) and the patch factor.

The NPU _preprocess patch in sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/modules/qwen_vl_processor.py still called resize() with the old signature: image= was swallowed by **kwargs while the required images/factor params were missing.

## Modifications

1. Image path: drop the manual smart_resize() call and invoke self.resize(images=..., size=size, resample=resample, factor=patch_size * merge_size), matching the upstream 5.19 _preprocess implementation.
2. Video path: drop the manual smart_resize() call and the 5D->4D fold/unfold around resize; call self.resize(videos=..., size=size, resample=resample, factor=..., temporal_factor=...) directly, since the new resize() handles the (B, T, C, H, W) tensor natively.
3. Remove the now-unused smart_resize / smart_resize (video) imports. The NPU-specific flattening logic (transform_patches_to_flatten, avoiding tensors > 8 dims on Ascend) is unchanged.

title: [NPU] Fix non-DSA prefill context parallel on the CP v2 strategy
body:
Fix non-DSA prefill context parallel (CP v2) for the generic Ascend attention backend.

Prefill CP is broken for every model that uses the generic Ascend attention
backend (Qwen3, Qwen3-MoE, ...) after the CP v1 runtime was removed. Two
defects remain in that path:

1. `_cp_allgather_and_save_kv_npu` still calls
   `cp_all_gather_rerange_kv_cache`, which is now an import-only shim that
   raises `ValueError: Prefill CP on HIP/NPU/MUSA is deprecated`. Route the KV
   write through the CP v2 strategy (`materialize_full_kv`), matching the
   `cp_active` branch of `flashattention_backend`.

2. `do_cp_attn_fia` hands `npu_fused_infer_attention_score` the physical query
   shard while advertising only the logical tokens in `actual_seq_lengths`.
   The model runner pads the shard to `per_rank_actual_token[0]` rows, so the
   cumulative sequence lengths no longer match the query row count and tiling
   fails with error 561002. Drop the pad rows before the op and re-append them
   to the output (mirrors the non-CP FIA path).

Also drops the now-unused `get_current_device_stream_fast` import (ruff F401).

Scope: only the non-DSA prefill CP path. DSA/GLM prefill CP already works
through their own backend and is unchanged.

Verified on Ascend A3 (CANN 9.1.0-a3), Qwen3-30B-A3B:
- bf16, TP=4 + MOE_DP=2 + ATTN_CP=2 + prefill CP zigzag, ASCEND_USE_FIA=1:
  GSM8K 100q/5-shot = 0.95 (CP off: 0.93-0.94).
- w8a8, same config: 0.90-0.92 (CP off: 0.80-0.84).
- Qwen3-0.6B: first-token logprobs match a non-CP run across 21 prompt lengths
  and a bs=4 batch; repeating the CP run reproduces identical output.
- Unit tests (test_npu_prefill_cp_backend.py, CPU-only): 8/8 OK.

title: Re-verify full-set GSM8K fix for DeepEP DeepSeek-V2 tests on cann9.1.0-a3-B081
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for the DeepEP DeepSeek-V2 cases, both **verified on `cann9.1.0-a3-B083` (run [38109809944](https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/actions/runs/38109809944), a3-8, both cases in full: 4/4 tests OK)**:

1. **Flaky gsm8k accuracy gate** (original ticket, B071/B072): `0.33 / 0.31 not >= 0.34`
2. **mmlu always 0.000** (found during verification; same symptom as the Aug 12 ticket whose fix was never synced to these cases)

Current state: test-case fixes only, across 4 commits (a6eec00742, 94c5e3e6c2, 091566399b). The `single-test-npu.yml` changes are verification-only and **will be reverted after review**.

---

## Fix 1: full-set GSM8K (num_questions = None)

Root cause: `GSM8KAscendMixin.num_questions = 200` samples the **first 200** GSM8K questions, a noisy gate:

- B071 same-config, 200-question prefix: **0.310 / 0.340** -- gate flips run to run
- B071 same-config, full set: **0.3592 (472/1314) / 0.3607 (474/1314)** -- stable above 0.34
- The 200-question prefix is harder than average (same run: full 0.3592 vs prefix 0.3100; the extra 1114 questions score 0.3680)
- No invalid answers / empty responses / failed requests

Both cases get `num_questions = None` (all 1314 questions, few-shot excluded by the eval). Threshold stays 0.34.

---

## Fix 2: mmlu zero-shot (drop num_shots=5, baseline 0.58 -> 0.38)

`test_mmlu` scored **0.000 across all categories** in verification run [37776934235](https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/actions/runs/37776934235) -- its first-ever real execution (previously masked by the CI failfast because test_gsm8k always failed first). Random guessing scores ~0.25, so 0.0 means systematic answer-extraction failure.

Root cause (consistent with the Aug 12 ticket "mmlu precision 0" on the same cases, whose fix was never carried over): with `num_shots=5`, `MMLUEval` prepends five few-shot examples rendered by `format_multichoice_question_example` -- which is the QUERY template **without the answer**. The model receives six consecutive unanswered questions; the completion-style continuation does not follow the `Answer: $LETTER` contract and the answer regex fails for every question.

Fix (as prescribed by the Aug 12 ticket, applied to both cases):

- drop `num_shots=5` from the eval args -> single-question zero-shot template
- `expect_score` 0.58 -> 0.38 (baseline re-measured on GPU per the ticket; NPU measured higher than GPU)

---

## Final verification (cann9.1.0-a3-B083, run [38109809944](https://github.com/Ascend/sglang/actions/runs/38109809944))

| case | gsm8k (full 1314, >= 0.34) | mmlu (0-shot 128, > 0.38) | tests time |
|---|---|---|---|
| deepep auto | **0.3417** | **0.4609** | 1254s |
| deepep low_latency | **0.3501** | **0.4688** | 926s |

**4/4 tests OK.** mmlu went from 0.000 (broken 5-shot extraction) to 0.461/0.469, consistent with the Aug 12 ticket's finding that NPU scores higher than the 0.38 GPU baseline.

Notes:

- **gsm8k margin is thin on B083** (auto 0.3417 vs 0.34, ~2 questions). Full-set scores across images/runs so far: B071 0.3592/0.3607, B081 0.3577/0.3539, B083 0.3417/0.3501. All pass, but the full-set gate variance (~+-0.01) is wider than the developer's two B071 runs suggested; reviewers may want to consider whether 0.34 leaves enough headroom.
- auto-case est_time bumped 1200 -> 1500: measured 1269s tests-only on B083 (0-shot mmlu generates longer than the truncated 5-shot).

---

## Verification-setup notes (workflow, to be reverted)

- The six consecutive `ImagePullBackOff` failures during verification (runs 37785710869 / 37788053860 / 37790302556 / 37793215877 / 37817218278 / 38041063456) were **not** an infrastructure outage: the SWR domain had been mistyped as `swr.cn-south-west-2` (extra hyphen) in the verification yml. With the correct `swr.cn-southwest-2`, the pull succeeded on the first try (run 38109809944). The a3-8 pool was never broken.

## Summary

Original failure (full-test run 35516918693, job 106094326260, cann9.1.0-a3-B070, 2026-09-20):

```
AssertionError: 153.51178041496112 not greater than or equal to 160.0
```

Root cause: the old `test_tokenizer_batch_encode_throughput_improvement` measured **single-request decode throughput** (one 256-token generation, threshold 200*0.8=160 tok/s), which is unrelated to `--enable-tokenizer-batch-encode` (the parameter only batches tokenization of input texts). Measured decode throughput on B070 was 107/153 tok/s across both retries; `test_gsm8k` passed (0.41 >= 0.38). This is a test design mismatch, not a functional bug.

## Changes (test case only)

- Benchmark per-prompt tokenization latency directly in the test process: sequential encode (`tokenizer([t])` per prompt, flag-off behavior) vs batch encode (`tokenizer(texts)`, flag-on behavior), input scale aligned with community v0.5.5 `benchmark/benchmark_batch/benchmark_batch.py` (10 requests x 8 prompts x 32000 tokens, seeded for reproducibility)
- Assert batch mode has lower avg per-prompt latency (relative comparison, no environment-sensitive absolute threshold)
- `test_gsm8k` launches a dp=2 server with the flag enabled for end-to-end correctness (score >= 0.38)

- Keep the modelscope weights path from `test_ascend_utils` instead of the hardcoded `/home/weights/Qwen3-0.6B` (does not exist on CI runners)
- Store the launched server process on the class attribute so `tearDownClass` kills it via `terminate_and_kill_process_tree` (the developer flagged the residual-process concern)

title: [DSpark][NPU] Fix attn_tp > 1 draft wo_b all_reduce group
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
DSpark speculative decoding with a DeepSeek-V4 (MoE) draft supports DP attention
(`attn_tp_size < tp_size`) on Ascend NPU, but the draft attention's output
projection `wo_b` reduced its partial results over the wrong process group,
which corrupted the draft output and collapsed the accept rate to ~0.

`DSparkAttention` (`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_dspark.py`) subclasses
`MqaAttentionBase` and hard-codes `wo_b_reduce_results=True`, overriding the
base's default `reduce_results = (attn_tp_size == tp_size and attn_tp_size > 1)`.
As a result, under DP attention (`attn_tp_size < tp_size`) `wo_b` still performed
a row-parallel all-reduce, but over the **full DP × TP** group, while its weight
is sharded over the **attn-TP** group only. That summed partial outputs that
belong to different DP ranks' _different_ batches, so the draft attention output
was garbage and the accept rate collapsed to ~0.

A guard in `DSparkWorkerV2` rejected this whole configuration
(`attn_tp > 1` + DP attention + MoE draft), which blocked the feature on NPU.

(Note: the guard's error string referred to the "MoE-under-DP all-reduce", but
the actual corruption was the draft attention's `wo_b` reduce group; the draft
MoE path itself handles `attn_tp > 1` via `_dp_gather_via_all_gather`.)

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

1. `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`
   - `MqaAttentionBase.wo_b` now passes
     `use_dp_attention_reduce=is_dp_attention_enabled()`, so its row-parallel
     all-reduce runs over the attn-TP group (`get_parallel().attn_tp_group`)
     when DP attention is enabled, matching the weight sharding.
   - `DSparkAttention.forward` calls `self.wo_b(...)` directly (it does not use
     `_project_wo_b`), so this single flag fixes the draft reduce with no
     double-reduce.

2. `python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py`
   - Allow the `attn_tp > 1` MoE-draft + DP-attention configuration on NPU by
     adding `and not _is_npu` to the guard. CUDA/ROCm still reject it.

3. `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_dsv4_backend.py`
   - Pad the draft `ori_sparse_indices` tail with `-1` ("skip") up to the
     attn-TP-padded token count, matching `out_cache_loc`
     (`prepare_mlp_sync_batch` pads the query to an attn_tp multiple, but
     `seq_lens` is not).

title: [NPU][HiCache] Support DeepSeek V4 L3 with MemCache
body:
## Motivation

Enable DeepSeek V4 NPU HiCache L3 backup and restore through the existing `npu_memcache` backend on `release/2026930`.

Port of https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39784 at `66a05899d65711baeaf945e40c80a188fae73334`, based on release commit `abc87e21637e55bd23a5a1863a0cda3bb4d84029`.

## Modifications

- Add C128 storage transfers, complete-group alignment, and physical-pool key handling while keeping the FULL anchor logical.
- Keep C128-specific behavior in the NPU component. Shared transfer hooks use a default one-to-one page mapping; the alignment hook passes a node ID, so other components do not call the Python-only `node_by_id()` interface.
- Initialize MemCache eagerly. For NPU DSV4 with `npu_memcache`, run HCCL and custom AiCPU initialization before cache construction, reusing the existing attention metadata builder.
- Add MemCache storage-contract and restore regression tests, and document the supported DSV4 layout/mode.

The port contains the same 10 changed files as the upstream PR, in one commit on the release branch. It preserves the release branch's existing DSpark attention routing.

## Accuracy Tests

Local checks on this release port:

title: [NPU][HiCache] Fix MLA host pool crash with MTP draft pools
body:
MLATokenToKVPoolHost unconditionally built the packed target+draft device pointer tables (torch.cat over pool.data_ptrs) whenever MTP draft device pools were present. NPUMLATokenToKVPool deliberately skips the base MLATokenToKVPool __init__ and keeps contiguous k/v buffers instead of the CUDA-style per-layer data_ptrs/kv_buffer tables, so scheduler startup crashed with AttributeError: 'NPUMLATokenToKVPool' object has no attribute 'data_ptrs' once HiCache offload was combined with MTP draft layers.

Extract the packed-table build into an overridable _init_packed_device_transfer_buffers hook and add a get_mla_host_pool_cls factory (mirroring get_mha_host_pool_cls) that dispatches to a new NPUMLATokenToKVPoolHost subclass on NPU. The subclass skips the packed build: those tables are only consumed by the kernel/direct IO backends (_resolve_device_transfer_buffers), which kernel_ascend short-circuits. Also switch the TensorCast MLA adapter check from 'is' to isinstance so the NPU subclass is recognized.

title: Ascend dspark0924 dspark
body:
## Motivation

Enable GLM-5.2 DSpark with a Speculators-format dense BF16 draft and a ModelSlim QuaRot target on Ascend NPU. The draft export needs configuration translation, and its original-coordinate vocabulary and target-feature projection must remain compatible with the rotated target.

This PR targets static DSpark. It does not change the target checkpoint, draft training, sampling policy, or DSpark acceptance algorithm. Compact mode support is outside this PR.

Depends on [sgl-kernel-npu #791](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/791) for head_dim=192. Development testing uses the candidate `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py` through a process-local Python package overlay; the binary library and other modules remain from the image-installed `sgl-kernel-npu` package. A released package version or reproducible image that includes #791 for normal installation is still **TODO**; the existing image is not claimed to contain this change.

## Modifications

- In `configs/speculators.py`, translate a copy of the loaded configuration dictionary: flatten `transformer_layer_config`, preserve `architectures=["DSparkDraftModel"]`, set `model_type="qwen3"`, derive `target_layer_ids` from the export's auxiliary IDs, and reject conflicting aliases. Remove the nested decoder and incompatible `auto_map` from the copy so reloading the normalized layout does not translate IDs again. The source JSON is not rewritten.
- Connect this translation through the explicit `_try_load_speculators_qwen3_dense_config` branch in the existing HF parser. Build a `Qwen3Config` for the draft's decoder parameters while keeping `DSparkDraftModel` as the model implementation; route LongCat through its separate `_try_load_longcat_config` branch, then use the ordinary `AutoConfig` fallback. The normalization function is named `normalize_speculators_qwen3_dense_dspark_config` so the supported schema and decoder boundary are visible at the call site.
- Add opt-in boolean `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true` for an NPU GLM DSA ModelSlim QuaRot target with an unquantized dense draft whose weights remain in the original/unrotated coordinates. `DSparkWorkerV2.__init__` scopes the validated target metadata to draft construction. The default is `false`; `true` enables checkpoint-local vocabulary modules and load-time FC correction, while `false` preserves the existing shared-vocabulary loading path. An enabled switch that cannot be applied emits a clear warning; incomplete QuaRot metadata remains a startup error.
- In `DSparkDraftMixin`, create and load the draft's own embedding/LM head through the existing loader. `DraftBlockProposer.propose` selects that embedding for the anchor-sampling path as well, keeping the external and in-model embedding entry points consistent.
- During `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights`, `fold_glm_dspark_fc` converts each newly read FC block as `F_i @ Q` on CPU in FP32 and stores the original dtype. Validate the initial vocabulary/FC inputs; retain existing loader requirements on later reloads. Conversion changes the loaded tensor, not the checkpoint file.
- Before constructing an enabled QuaRot draft, reject draft load formats that can bypass `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights()`. Startup logs report the requested/effective QuaRot state, the resolved Q path, and whether the draft-local embedding and LM head are active.
- Add regression coverage for configuration, quantization selection, loading, QuaRot conversion, vocabulary parallelism and embedding dispatch in eight CPU-registered test files.

The DFlash backbone and NPU fused-QKV call, DSpark proposal/verification/commit flow, and source checkpoints are preserved. The stored Q is not assumed to have an exact floating-point inverse.

## Supported Pairing and Startup

This switch is a deployment contract, not automatic checkpoint detection:

| Target/draft pairing | Setting | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| NPU GLM DSA ModelSlim target with QuaRot metadata + unquantized dense draft in its original/unrotated coordinates | `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true` | Load draft-local embedding/LM head and fold each target-feature FC input block as `F_i @ Q` during loading. |
| Native/no-QuaRot target + coordinate-compatible draft | unset or `false` | Preserve the existing shared target embedding/LM-head path and do not fold the draft FC. |
| Draft already converted into the target's rotated coordinates | unset or `false` | Avoid applying the rotation twice. |
| W4A8 or another target artifact without ModelSlim QuaRot metadata | unset or `false` | No QuaRot draft correction is required by this adapter. |

The enabled path currently supports the dense `DSparkDraftModel` integration only. It does not claim automatic support for arbitrary Speculators exports, MoE drafts, non-GLM targets, quantized drafts, or a different rotation convention. The runtime validates the GLM DSA architecture, ModelSlim configuration, `is_rot_used`, rotation path/tensor and hidden width. If `true` is set outside the supported NPU/dense/target path, the service logs that the requested adaptation was not applied.

Draft load-format support is intentionally narrow. The QuaRot path relies on `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights()` both to fold the FC as `F_i @ Q` and to verify that the draft-local embedding, LM head and FC were all loaded. With `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true`, startup accepts only the verified `auto`, `pt`, `safetensors`, `fastsafetensors`, `npcache`, and `mistral` draft formats. It fails before draft construction for formats such as `dummy`, `sharded_state`, `presharded`, `remote`, and `remote_instance`, and when IPC weight-cache loading is enabled, because those paths can bypass the required transformation/check entry point. This PR does not claim compatibility with arbitrary `--speculative-draft-load-format` values.

On NPU DSpark startup, the runtime logs `requested`, effective `enabled`, the resolved `q_path`, and the effective `draft_local_embedding` / `draft_local_lm_head` booleans. This distinguishes an explicitly requested adapter from one that was actually installed after target/draft validation.

Example:

```bash
SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true \
python -m sglang.launch_server ...
```

Accepted true values follow `EnvBool` (`true`, `1`, `yes`, or `y`, case-insensitive); false values are `false`, `0`, `no`, or `n`. The former string value `original` is not valid.

## Validation

## Modifications

- During `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights`, `fold_glm_dspark_fc` converts each newly read FC block as `F_i @ Q` on CPU in FP32 and stores the original dtype. | Target/draft pairing | Setting | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| NPU GLM DSA ModelSlim target with QuaRot metadata + unquantized dense draft in its original/unrotated coordinates | `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true` | Load draft-local embedding/LM head and fold each target-feature FC input block as `F_i @ Q` during loading. |
| Native/no-QuaRot target + coordinate-compatible draft | unset or `false` | Preserve the existing shared target embedding/LM-head path and do not fold the draft FC. |
| Draft already converted into the target's rotated coordinates | unset or `false` | Avoid applying the rotation twice. |
| W4A8 or another target artifact without ModelSlim QuaRot metadata | unset or `false` | No QuaRot draft correction is required by this adapter. |

The enabled path currently supports the dense `DSparkDraftModel` integration only. It does not claim automatic support for arbitrary Speculators exports, MoE drafts, non-GLM targets, quantized drafts, or a different rotation convention. The runtime validates the GLM DSA architecture, ModelSlim configuration, `is_rot_used`, rotation path/tensor and hidden width. Draft load-format support is intentionally narrow. The QuaRot path relies on `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights()` both to fold the FC as `F_i @ Q` and to verify that the draft-local embedding, LM head and FC were all loaded. Example:

```bash
SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true \
python -m sglang.launch_server ...
```

Accepted true values follow `EnvBool` (`true`, `1`, `yes`, or `y`, case-insensitive); false values are `false`, `0`, `no`, or `n`. The former string value `original` is not valid.

title: [NPU][GLM5.2] support dsa pcp with interleave & zigzag (release/2026930)
body:
## Summary

Adapt GLM-5.2 (GlmMoeDsa) DSA prefill context parallelism to the CP V2 strategy flow, mirroring the DSV4 CP V2 support merged in #39427. After CP V1 was deprecated upstream, the NPU DSA path still referenced removed V1 metadata fields and could no longer run with --enable-prefill-cp.

## Changes

- **ascend_backend.py**: add prepare_dsa_cp_metadata which builds per-token local metadata for the Ascend sparse kernels (q/kv lengths from sharded local positions, per-token block-table rows selected by local batch ids); rewrite do_cp_balance_attn to a single npu_sparse_flash_attention call on the strategy-sharded local Q (no V1 prev/next balance split).
- **dsa_npu_indexer.py**: read V2 local metadata instead of the removed V1 attn_cp_metadata fields (actual_seq_q_prev_tensor / kv_len_prev_tensor / ...); rewrite do_npu_cp_balance_indexer as a single npu_lightning_indexer call.
- **deepseek_v2.py**: prepare DSA CP metadata at the inner-model entry (the eager CP runner invokes DeepseekV2Model directly); restore rebuild_cp_kv_cache, gathering the rank-local latent KV into full sequence order via cp_gather_full_sequence_states.
- **forward_mha.py**: on NPU with CP active, gather kv_a/k_pe to full sequence order before writing, since out_cache_loc spans the full sequence under CP V2.
- **unit tests**: add `test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` covering the zigzag/interleave block layout, local row selection, padding alignment, the `is_cp_active` gate, and the GLM DSA layer-split helpers.

The first commit fixes the attn_cp_tp_broadcast_pyobj broadcast order for attn-CP > 1 (broadcast along the attn-TP 0 line first, then TP).

## Testing

Full-model verification on a 4-node Ascend 910B3 cluster (32 NPUs/node) with GLM-5.2-w8a8 (GlmMoeDsa) in PD disaggregation:

- **Prefill** (2 nodes, 209/212): `--tp-size 8 --pp-size 4 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 --mem-fraction-static 0.88`, NEXTN spec (num-steps 1, draft 2)
- **Decode** (2 nodes, 216/217): `--tp-size 32 --dp-size 32 --ep-size 32`, NEXTN spec (num-steps 3, draft 4)
- Key envs: `DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=2048`, `SGLANG_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=18,20,24,16`, `SGLANG_DISAGGREGATION_ALL_CP_RANKS_TRANSFER=1`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1`, `MALLOC_CHECK_=3`
- Client: vllm bench serve through the sglang PD router (16 prompts, concurrency 4, input 65536 / output 2500)

### Throughput / latency results

| config | result | TTFT mean / median / P99 | TPOT | throughput |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| zigzag + chunk 4096 | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 9.45s / 5.85s / 26.05s | 26.89 ms | 3370 tok/s |
| interleave + chunk 8192 (fixed len) | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 9.12s / 6.08s / 20.05s | 25.70 ms | 3570 tok/s |
| interleave + chunk 8192 (variable input 40960–90112) | :white_check_mark: 16/16 | 7.82s / 6.94s / 15.53s | 25.85 ms | 3550 tok/s |

The zigzag + chunk 8192 crash is a deep_ep CAM dispatch buffer overflow (`HCCL_BUFFSIZE is too SMALL`, 3304MB needed > 2048MB) triggered when a pass dispatches the whole 8076-token batch per rank; chunk 4096 caps the per-rank dispatch at ~1.78GB. Interleave keeps CP active on every pass (1024 tokens/rank, ~604MB), so it is safe with chunk 8192.

### Accuracy (gpqa_diamond)

evalscope + LLM-judge against the PD router: **166/174 judged correct = 95.40%** (174 of 198 samples were judged before the run was stopped; 23 samples had timed out at the 900s client timeout during inference and 1 was left unjudged. CI gate is 91.2%.)

### Unit tests

`test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` — **21/21 passed** (CPU, no NPU needed):

```
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py -v
```

```bash
# Same script on all 4 nodes; the role is picked from the local IP.
#   prefill (2p): 192.168.25.209, 192.168.25.212   tp8 x pp4 = 32 cards

sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0 >/dev/null 2>&1

        export SGLANG_DISAGG_PREFILL_EARLY_SEND_CACHED_PREFIX=1

          --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
          --disaggregation-mode prefill \
          --tp-size 8 --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave \
          --nnodes 2 --node-rank "$i" --dist-init-addr "${P_IP[0]}:5000" \
          --mem-fraction-static 0.88 \
          --attention-backend ascend --device npu --quantization modelslim \
          --disaggregation-transfer-backend ascend \
          --max-running-requests 64 \
          --served-model-name glm-5 \
          --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
          --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
```

## Summary

Port of sgl-project/sglang#40165 (GLM-5.2 DSA prefill context parallelism with interleave & zigzag) onto the `release/2026930` branch. This PR carries **only the GLM-5.2 adaptation commits** (main adaptation + unit tests) — no other upstream commits are included.

## Changes

- **ascend_backend.py**: add `prepare_dsa_cp_metadata` which builds per-token local metadata for the Ascend sparse kernels (q/kv lengths from sharded local positions, per-token block-table rows); rewrite `do_cp_balance_attn` to a single `npu_sparse_flash_attention` call on the strategy-sharded local Q (no V1 prev/next balance split).
- **dsa_npu_indexer.py**: read V2 local metadata instead of the removed V1 `attn_cp_metadata` fields; rewrite `do_npu_cp_balance_indexer` as a single `npu_lightning_indexer` call.
- **deepseek_v2.py / deepseek_nextn.py**: prepare DSA CP metadata at the inner-model entry (the eager CP runner invokes the inner model directly); restore `rebuild_cp_kv_cache`, gathering the rank-local latent KV into full sequence order via `cp_gather_full_sequence_states`.
- **forward_mha.py**: on NPU with CP active, gather kv_a/k_pe to full sequence order before writing, since `out_cache_loc` spans the full sequence under CP V2.
- **unit tests**: `test/registered/unit/layers/cp/test_dsa_cp_metadata.py` covering zigzag/interleave block layout, local row selection, padding alignment, the `is_cp_active` gate, and the GLM DSA layer-split helpers.

## Port notes for release/2026930

- Rebased cleanly onto `release/2026930` (HEAD `e3b41a477`): the CP V2 strategy framework (`layers/cp/`, `cp_gather_full_sequence_states`, `local_q_indices`, `is_dsa_enable_prefill_cp`) is already present in this release line.
- Two import-block context conflicts (in `ascend_backend.py` and `deepseek_nextn.py`) were resolved manually — the release branch has a few extra imports (e.g. `layers.dcp.layout`) that do not exist on main.
- The unit-test case for `interleave_rows_per_request` was dropped in this port because that helper does not exist on `release/2026930` (it was added to main later).
- Verified on an Ascend NPU container (same CANN/fa5cfd70 environment as the mainline PR):
  - `py_compile` clean on all 6 touched files;

## Testing

End-to-end validation on the mainline version of the same code was done in sgl-project/sglang#40165 (4-node 910B3 cluster, GLM-5.2-w8a8 PD disaggregation, tp8×pp4×attn-cp8 prefill):

title: [NPU] Support GLM-5.2 DSpark loading
body:
## Motivation

Enable GLM-5.2 DSpark with a Speculators-format dense BF16 draft and a ModelSlim QuaRot target on Ascend NPU. The draft export needs configuration translation, and its original-coordinate vocabulary and target-feature projection must remain compatible with the rotated target.

This PR targets static DSpark. It does not change the target checkpoint, draft training, sampling policy, or DSpark acceptance algorithm. Compact mode support is outside this PR.

Depends on [sgl-kernel-npu #791](https://github.com/sgl-project/sgl-kernel-npu/pull/791) for head_dim=192. Development testing uses the candidate `split_qkv_rmsnorm_rope.py` through a process-local Python package overlay; the binary library and other modules remain from the image-installed `sgl-kernel-npu` package. A released package version or reproducible image that includes #791 for normal installation is still **TODO**; the existing image is not claimed to contain this change.

## Modifications

- In `configs/speculators.py`, translate a copy of the loaded configuration dictionary: flatten `transformer_layer_config`, preserve `architectures=["DSparkDraftModel"]`, set `model_type="qwen3"`, derive `target_layer_ids` from the export's auxiliary IDs, and reject conflicting aliases. Remove the nested decoder and incompatible `auto_map` from the copy so reloading the normalized layout does not translate IDs again. The source JSON is not rewritten.
- Connect this translation through the explicit `_try_load_speculators_qwen3_dense_config` branch in the existing HF parser. Build a `Qwen3Config` for the draft's decoder parameters while keeping `DSparkDraftModel` as the model implementation; route LongCat through its separate `_try_load_longcat_config` branch, then use the ordinary `AutoConfig` fallback. The normalization function is named `normalize_speculators_qwen3_dense_dspark_config` so the supported schema and decoder boundary are visible at the call site.
- Add opt-in boolean `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true` for an NPU GLM DSA ModelSlim QuaRot target with an unquantized dense draft whose weights remain in the original/unrotated coordinates. `DSparkWorkerV2.__init__` scopes the validated target metadata to draft construction. The default is `false`; `true` enables checkpoint-local vocabulary modules and load-time FC correction, while `false` preserves the existing shared-vocabulary loading path. An enabled switch that cannot be applied emits a clear warning; incomplete QuaRot metadata remains a startup error.
- In `DSparkDraftMixin`, create and load the draft's own embedding/LM head through the existing loader. `DraftBlockProposer.propose` selects that embedding for the anchor-sampling path as well, keeping the external and in-model embedding entry points consistent.
- During `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights`, `fold_glm_dspark_fc` converts each newly read FC block as `F_i @ Q` on CPU in FP32 and stores the original dtype. Validate the initial vocabulary/FC inputs; retain existing loader requirements on later reloads. Conversion changes the loaded tensor, not the checkpoint file.
- Before constructing an enabled QuaRot draft, reject draft load formats that can bypass `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights()`. Startup logs report the requested/effective QuaRot state, the resolved Q path, and whether the draft-local embedding and LM head are active.
- Add regression coverage for configuration, quantization selection, loading, QuaRot conversion, vocabulary parallelism and embedding dispatch in eight CPU-registered test files.

The DFlash backbone and NPU fused-QKV call, DSpark proposal/verification/commit flow, and source checkpoints are preserved. The stored Q is not assumed to have an exact floating-point inverse.

## Supported Pairing and Startup

This switch is a deployment contract, not automatic checkpoint detection:

| Target/draft pairing | Setting | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| NPU GLM DSA ModelSlim target with QuaRot metadata + unquantized dense draft in its original/unrotated coordinates | `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true` | Load draft-local embedding/LM head and fold each target-feature FC input block as `F_i @ Q` during loading. |
| Native/no-QuaRot target + coordinate-compatible draft | unset or `false` | Preserve the existing shared target embedding/LM-head path and do not fold the draft FC. |
| Draft already converted into the target's rotated coordinates | unset or `false` | Avoid applying the rotation twice. |
| W4A8 or another target artifact without ModelSlim QuaRot metadata | unset or `false` | No QuaRot draft correction is required by this adapter. |

The enabled path currently supports the dense `DSparkDraftModel` integration only. It does not claim automatic support for arbitrary Speculators exports, MoE drafts, non-GLM targets, quantized drafts, or a different rotation convention. The runtime validates the GLM DSA architecture, ModelSlim configuration, `is_rot_used`, rotation path/tensor and hidden width. If `true` is set outside the supported NPU/dense/target path, the service logs that the requested adaptation was not applied.

Draft load-format support is intentionally narrow. The QuaRot path relies on `DSparkDraftMixin.load_weights()` both to fold the FC as `F_i @ Q` and to verify that the draft-local embedding, LM head and FC were all loaded. With `SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true`, startup accepts only the verified `auto`, `pt`, `safetensors`, `fastsafetensors`, `npcache`, and `mistral` draft formats. It fails before draft construction for formats such as `dummy`, `sharded_state`, `presharded`, `remote`, and `remote_instance`, and when IPC weight-cache loading is enabled, because those paths can bypass the required transformation/check entry point. This PR does not claim compatibility with arbitrary `--speculative-draft-load-format` values.

On NPU DSpark startup, the runtime logs `requested`, effective `enabled`, the resolved `q_path`, and the effective `draft_local_embedding` / `draft_local_lm_head` booleans. This distinguishes an explicitly requested adapter from one that was actually installed after target/draft validation.

Example:

```bash
SGLANG_NPU_GLM_DSPARK_APPLY_QUAROT_TO_DRAFT=true \
python -m sglang.launch_server ...
```

Accepted true values follow `EnvBool` (`true`, `1`, `yes`, or `y`, case-insensitive); false values are `false`, `0`, `no`, or `n`. The former string value `original` is not valid.

## Validation

Last tested PR head: `b448f591a96f58923e1aee81e80d938fa9e9130d`; merge base: `dc2157dcd62d5fb1bc5317fcf8765ebfcd8a8dad`.

**Local CPU: 119 tests and 108 subtests passed** across the eight affected test files on this final committed head. This includes the boolean environment interface, unsupported-loader fail-fast, effective-state logging, configuration translation, loading, FC folding, vocabulary parallelism, embedding dispatch, and existing `test_hf_transformers.py` regressions. Tests use CPU arithmetic, Gloo where applicable, selected NPU mocks, and the repository's macOS platform compatibility layer; this is not NPU execution or GitHub CI validation.

Targeted Ruff 0.15.1 formatting and lint passed for the affected files on the final head. `git diff --check` also passed.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=python HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest -q \
```

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable DeepSeek V4 DSpark speculative decoding on NPU Ascend 950 (arch35). The existing DSpark implementation only supported CUDA and older NPU (arch22). Arch35 hardware requires different sparse-attention operators, weight-loading strategies, and numerical compatibility workarounds. Several follow-up fixes address a regression where DSpark's unquantized `wo_a` path conflicted with the arch35 MXFP8 detection logic, plus NPU-specific numerical gaps.

## Modifications

- **arch35 DSpark sparse attention**: Added arch35-specific v2 sparse attention operators via a new `TorchOpLoader` extension; loaded during TP worker and DSpark draft worker initialization.
- **`wo_a` quantization fix**: `use_npu_arch35_mxfp8_wo_a()` now accepts a `wo_a_keeps_quant_config` parameter and returns `False` when DSpark explicitly disables `wo_a` quantization. This fixes a regression introduced by a previous commit that changed the assertion condition from `if fp8:` to `if quantize_wo_a:`, which caused an incorrect assertion on arch35 because DSpark's `wo_a` was not quantized. The model also caches this value instead of recomputing it at each call site.
- **DSpark stage configuration**: Added `_dspark_stage_config()` to apply draft-specific expert counts to draft stages and disable vision layers for text-only stages. Arch35 now falls back to standard vocabulary/fusion behavior instead of the arch31-specific path.
- **Weight loading**: Moved the NPU `weight_packed` → `weight` rename before stacked parameter mapping, eliminating duplicated branch logic.
- **NPU numerical compatibility**: Fall back to torch for commit-KV projection on NPU; replaced `exponential_()` (unsupported on NPU) with `uniform_ + log_ + neg_`.

body:
[NPU][CI] Add a5 test tasks (full-test + nightly) with tp-size halving on a5

Based on PR #1234 (`patch-14-validate`). Adds a5 (950) device tasks to the NPU full test and nightly pipelines, running the same testcases as a3 with half the cards.

## Mapping (a3 -> a5)

| a3 job | a5 job | runner |
|---|---|---|
| full-1-npu-a3 (170 regs) | full-1-npu-a5 | linux-amd64-a5-2 |
| full-2-npu-a3 (61 regs) | full-1-npu-a5 | linux-amd64-a5-2 |
| full-4-npu-a3 (45 regs) | full-2-npu-a5 | linux-amd64-a5-2 |
| full-8-npu-a3 (22 regs) | full-4-npu-a5 | linux-amd64-a5-4 |
| full-16-npu-a3 (28 regs) | full-8-npu-a5 | linux-amd64-a5-8 |

Same mapping for `nightly-*` suites. `full-1-npu-a5` (229 enabled cases) is split across 4 partitions.

## Changes

1. **Workflows**
   - `full-test-npu.yml`: `image_a5` input (default `cann9.1.0-950-B060`), 4 new a5 jobs, `check-all-jobs` updated
   - `nightly-test-npu.yml`: `image_a5` input/output, 4 new a5 jobs (plain runner labels `linux-amd64-a5-2/4/8`), result summary updated
   - `_npu-pr-test-stage.yml`: export `SGLANG_TEST_NPU_DEVICE_TYPE` from the `npu_device_type` input
2. **tp-size halving (central interception)**
   - `environ.py`: new test hook `SGLANG_TEST_NPU_DEVICE_TYPE = EnvStr(None)`
   - `test_utils.popen_launch_server`: when the hook is `a5`, halve `--tp-size` / `--tensor-parallel-size` (min 1) in `other_args`. All NPU launch paths (plain, PD-separated, e2e harnesses) go through this function. Local runs and a3/a2 jobs are unaffected (hook unset).
3. **Registrations (mechanical, 358 files)**
   - Every `register_npu_ci(suite="full-X-npu-a3"/"nightly-X-npu-a3", ...)` is mirrored by an identical a5-suite registration, preserving `est_time`, `nightly`, and `disabled`.
   - Verified: `sglang.test.ci.ci_register` parses all files with 0 errors; per-suite counts match the table above.
   - Reproducible transform script (run with `python -X utf8 add_a5_registrations.py`):

```python
import ast, glob, os, re

SUITE_MAP = {
    "full-1-npu-a3": "full-1-npu-a5", "full-2-npu-a3": "full-1-npu-a5",
    "full-4-npu-a3": "full-2-npu-a5", "full-8-npu-a3": "full-4-npu-a5",
    "full-16-npu-a3": "full-8-npu-a5",
    "nightly-1-npu-a3": "nightly-1-npu-a5", "nightly-2-npu-a3": "nightly-1-npu-a5",
    "nightly-4-npu-a3": "nightly-2-npu-a5", "nightly-8-npu-a3": "nightly-4-npu-a5",
    "nightly-16-npu-a3": "nightly-8-npu-a5",
}

for path in glob.glob("test/registered/npu/**/*.py", recursive=True):
    if os.path.basename(path) in ("conftest.py", "__init__.py"):
        continue
    source = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()
    lines = source.split("\n")
    tree = ast.parse(source, filename=path)
    calls = [
        (s, next(kw.value.value for kw in s.value.keywords if kw.arg == "suite"))
        for s in tree.body
        if isinstance(s, ast.Expr) and isinstance(s.value, ast.Call)
        and isinstance(s.value.func, ast.Name) and s.value.func.id == "register_npu_ci"
        and any(kw.arg == "suite" and kw.value.value in SUITE_MAP for kw in s.value.keywords)
    ]
    if not calls:
        continue
    insertions = []
    for stmt, suite in calls:
        seg = "\n".join(lines[stmt.lineno - 1:stmt.end_lineno])
        new_seg = seg.replace(f'"{suite}"', f'"{SUITE_MAP[suite]}"', 1)
        indent = re.match(r"[ \t]*", seg).group(0)
        insertions.append((stmt.end_lineno, f"{indent}{new_seg}"))
    out, pending = [], sorted(insertions)
    for idx, line in enumerate(lines):
        out.append(line)
        while pending and pending[0][0] == idx + 1:
            out.append(pending.pop(0)[1])
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="").write("\n".join(out))
```

## Notes

- a5 est_time reuses the a3 values (partitioning is est-based; full-1-npu-a5 uses 4 partitions).
- perf (800t) / acc suites and multi-node e2e remain a3-only for now.

title: [NPU] Port Kimi-K3 fixes and ordinary MLA NZ support to PoC_20260831
body:
This ports the selected hanwlax changes from `zhaozx-cn/sglang:a5-k3-0828` onto `Ascend/sglang:PoC_20260831` (base `371e6feb4459c88ade962e97f527855e43d92734`).

Ordinary MLA can write FIA NZ cache without enabling MLAPO. Cached prefix pages are unpacked back to logical token order before projection in **both** prefix-attention paths present on the target branch, including Ring MLA. The Kimi-K3 changes also preserve attention-TP collectives on the current stream while overlapping the shared MLP, load full-rank QKVG shards for ModelSlim/DP attention, select DSpark FIAS V2 with matching graph metadata updates, and use the NPU chain sampler's random-buffer stride.

### Selected source changes

| Source commit | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `f3ca9cb559` | Shared-expert MLP overlap with collectives on the current stream |
| `6d48f564a6`, `6ffc661d88` | Full-rank QKVG construction, mapping and weight loading |
| `8491b10adf` | Opt-in DSpark FIAS V2 and update-before-replay ordering |
| `f5d724b641` | DeepEP low-latency MXFP8 dispatch; normal dispatch stays BF16 |
| `c4ab122939` | NPU chain sampling and candidate-width random rows |
| `eac6e6b985` | Required NZ integration dependency |
| `17f7b8b0f4` | Logical MLA prefix reads from NZ storage |

**Excluded:** `ff2f4caf69` (SiTU + MXFP8 quantization fusion). No `NPUSituMXFP8Quant`, `situ_mxfp8_quant` import, or fused-SiTU environment switch is introduced. The independent DeepEP dispatch correction is retained.

### Coverage

UTs cover ND/NZ page ordering and repeated/empty selections; cross-page partial writes, overwrite, empty writes, noncontiguous input, combined-KV dtype conversion, FP8 byte storage and layer offsets; NZ without MLAPO; QKVG shard loading; shared-stream collective ordering; DeepEP dispatch selection, quantization-mode reset and legacy completion APIs; NPU/CUDA sampling strides; FIAS V2 query layout, padding and empty DP ranks; and graph handler selection/update ordering, list/tensor metadata compatibility and multistep graph selection.

Three registered NPU DTs cover:
- Real NZ scatter + FIAS V2 against a PyTorch attention reference, including graph replay across page boundaries with changing KV lengths.
- DSpark chain sampling with full acceptance, immediate rejection and partial rejection in different batch rows.
- DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite serving with MLAPO disabled: ND/NZ, chunked prefill, cached-prefix reuse, unequal batched suffixes and decode graphs.

### Validation and remaining work

- Passed: syntax compilation of all 24 changed Python files, targeted Ruff checks/formatting, whitespace checks and CI-registration checks.
- Passed: **26 isolated CPU logic tests** using cached CPU PyTorch. The harness executes selected production definitions and test bodies with unavailable infrastructure dependencies stubbed; this is **not** a full SGLang import/UT run.
- Negative controls caught raw NZ prefix gathers, the old sampling stride, replay-before-update ordering and the old QKVG loader gate.
- **Not run:** standard complete-environment UT execution and NPU DTs. The local environment lacks the full SGLang dependencies (`orjson` is the first import blocker), and the checked NPU host was unreachable. No device accuracy or performance claim is made. Kept as draft pending these checks.

Device commands from an Ascend environment with this checkout installed:

```bash
python3 test/registered/npu/test_npu_dspark_fias_v2_nz.py
python3 test/registered/npu/test_npu_dspark_chain_sampling.py
python3 test/registered/npu/basic_function/HiCache/test_npu_mla_nz_prefix.py
```

The FIAS V2 DT requires the matching torch_npu V2 graph-update handler; A5 MXFP8 dispatch validation requires the matching DeepEP quant_mode API.

title: [Bug] [NPU] UB overflow in mamba_state_update_triton when running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with NEXTN speculative decoding
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug


````
Running Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (qwen3_5, hybrid GDN + MoE) with NEXTN speculative decoding on Ascend 910C, the server dies during startup: the sgl-kernel-npu Triton kernel `mamba_state_update_triton.py` fails BiShengHIR compilation with a UB overflow:

```
triton.compiler.errors.MLIRCompilationError:
[ConvertLinalgRToBinary] encounters error:
loc(".../sgl_kernel_npu/mamba/mamba_state_update_triton.py":21:0): error: Failed to run BiShengHIR pipeline
loc(".../sgl_kernel_npu/mamba/mamba_state_update_triton.py":21:0): error: ub overflow, requires 2097152 bits while 1572864 bits available! (possible reason: tiling basic block is too large or block number is more than what user expect due to multi-buffer feature is enabled and some ops need extra local buffer.)
```

This is the same UB-overflow class as sgl-project/sglang#25330 (`move_cache_dynamic_last_kernel_h_block`, 910B3 / CANN 8.5.0), which was closed by the stale-bot without a fix. Our data shows it persists on the newest stack (910C / CANN 9.0.0 / torch_npu 2.10) and also hits the plain `mamba_state_update` path (kernel line 21), i.e. it is not specific to the `move_cache_dynamic_last_kernel_h_block` variant.

The identical server configuration **without** the speculative flags ran an 18-cell benchmark sweep with zero failures, so the failure is specific to the MTP draft path.
````

### Reproduction

````
```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B --dtype bfloat16 --trust-remote-code \
  --device npu --attention-backend ascend --tp-size 2 --port 30000 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16 32 \
  --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 2 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4
```

Model: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (BF16). The server never becomes healthy; startup aborts after the kernel compile failure.
````

````
Python: 3.11.15
NPU available: True
NPU 0,1: Ascend910C (A3 node, 2 dies x 64 GB HBM)
CANN: 9.0.0 (official container image layout cann-9.0.0)
````

2. **Add new model accuracy regression cases.** Introduce GSM8K accuracy baselines for three models: IBM Granite-4.0-micro, Tencent Hunyuan Hy3, and Poolside Laguna-XS.2. Also migrate the transcription test from Whisper to Qwen3-ASR (retaining the `whisper` model alias).

  - Rename tests: `test_auto_detect_*` → `test_language_omitted_*`. Remove language-detection assertions; focus on non-empty output and no leakage of special tokens (e.g., `<|asr|>`). Add delta-cleanup validation for streaming scenarios.
